hints: A tree has a unique path between every pair of nodes.
Run a traversal from any node to find a farthest node a.
Run a second traversal from a; its farthest distance is the tree diameter.
analogy: Walk from an arbitrary point to the end of the tree's longest path, then walk from that end to the other.
example: On a path of five nodes, two traversals find endpoints at distance 4.
algorithm: Run BFS/DFS from any vertex to find farthest a; traverse again from a and take the maximum distance.
correctness: A farthest vertex from an arbitrary tree node is an endpoint of some diameter; the second sweep reaches the opposite endpoint and measures the longest path.
